title: How extreme rain is putting orangutans at risk
description:
Orangutans are the world’s most endangered apes and they’re now even closer to extinction. They live on two islands in southeast Asia: Sumatra and Borneo. In November, an extreme weather event in the area killed more than 1,000 people there, plus about 7% of the world’s rarest type of orangutan according to a new study.

BBC Climate and Science reporter Georgina Rannard takes us through how orangutans are being pushed towards extinction and what some countries and charities are doing to protect them.

We also hear from a conservationist making an effort to save the species.

summaryZh: 本集談及紅毛猩猩（人猿）面臨的急迫滅絕風險。牠們分布在蘇門答臘和婆羅洲，過去一百年野外族群從約 230,000 隻驟減，目前婆羅洲約 104,000 隻、蘇門答臘約 14,000 隻、塔帕努利約 800 隻；平均每年約被殺 2,000 至 3,000 隻，若每年損失 1% 即可能走向滅絕。主要威脅包括為種植棕櫚油而大規模砍伐與放火、採礦（含近期金礦開發）、水力發電與紙漿伐林，以及幼獸被捕做非法寵物交易或因人類衝突遭殺害。去年 11 月的極端降雨與土石流造成約 1,000 人死亡，也奪走約 58 隻塔帕努利紅毛猩猩（約占其族群的 7%），顯示極端氣候會加劇瀕危程度。節目也介紹保育作法：設立受保護棲地、族群繁殖與基因保護，以及以資金補償換取保留森林等政策，並呼籲停止在塔帕努利棲地興建水壩或採礦等基礎建設以免加速滅絕。
summaryEn: The episode outlines how orangutans — literally “people of the forest” — are increasingly close to extinction. They live in the trees on Sumatra and Borneo; a century ago about 230,000 existed in the wild, today there are roughly 104,000 Bornean, 14,000 Sumatran and only about 800 Tapanuli orangutans. Major threats are habitat loss from palm oil expansion, logging, mining (including proposed gold mines), hydropower projects, and illegal pet trade and human–wildlife conflict; on average 2,000–3,000 orangutans are killed each year. An extreme rainfall event in November killed over 1,000 people and about 58 Tapanuli orangutans (around 7% of that species), illustrating how extreme weather can further push small populations toward extinction. Conservation measures discussed include protected habitats, breeding and genetic programs, payments to keep forests standing, and calls to halt infrastructure projects in critical orangutan habitat.
